# Tinkerdeck

> A Windows desktop app that groups a project's terminals (dev servers, databases, shells) into apps you can start, stop and watch. It has a command line (`tdk`) and an MCP server so an LLM can run and observe local development apps cheaply.

Tinkerdeck runs on the user's own PC. Use it to start a project's servers, wait until they are ready, read their logs, run one-off commands, and work with git, without opening terminals yourself.

The complete, exact reference for every tool and parameter is `README-LLM.md`, installed next to `tdk.exe` and printed by `tdk llms`. This file is the short version.

## Connect (MCP, stdio)

- Command: `tdk`   Arguments: `mcp`   (full path: `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Programs\Tinkerdeck\tdk.exe`)
- Register with every installed LLM client at once: `tdk mcp install` (Claude Code, Claude Desktop, Cursor, Windsurf, VS Code, Gemini CLI, opencode). Check with `tdk mcp status`. Snippet for other clients: `tdk mcp config`.
- If the app is not running, `tdk` starts it hidden. No API key, no network: it listens on 127.0.0.1 only, behind a per-launch token.

## Tools (14)

- `td_status`: all apps and terminal states in one short call. Params: `git` (add branches), `since` (a previous `rev`; same state answers "unchanged"). Start here.
- `td_up`: start every terminal of an app in order and wait until each is READY or one fails. Params: `app`, `wait` (default true), `timeout_s`. Ready = its `readyUrl` (local) answers, or its output has its `readyPattern`, or it stayed up 2 s.
- `td_down`: stop every terminal of an app.
- `td_start` / `td_stop` / `td_restart`: one terminal, or `console` for a shell (`console:2`; `shell`: powershell.exe, pwsh.exe, cmd.exe, gitbash, wsl.exe).
- `td_logs`: plain-text output (no colour codes). Params: `lines`, `since` (cursor), `new` (only unseen output), `grep` (a|b), `context`, `errors`, `dedupe`, `brief`.
- `td_wait`: block until a terminal prints a `pattern`, exits, or is running (`until`, `timeout_s`). Use instead of polling logs.
- `td_send`: type into a running terminal (`text`, `enter`).
- `td_run`: run one command in the app's folder with a timeout; the reply is brief by default: exit code, then for test/build runners (vitest, jest, dotnet, cargo, pytest, go, tsc, MSBuild, rustc) counts plus only the failures. Params: `command`, `cwd`, `shell`, `timeout_s`, `lines`, `format` (brief|full), `grep`, `context`, `errors`, `dedupe`.
- `td_git`: `op` = status, branches, log, switch, commit, fetch, pull (fast-forward only), push (never forces), sync; params `branch`, `message`, `paths`, `all`, `limit`.
- `td_add` / `td_detect`: add a project folder (terminals detected from npm scripts, dotnet, docker compose, cargo, go, python) or preview what would be.
- `td_shells`: shells installed on this machine.

## Cheap workflow

1. `td_status`  2. `td_up` (waits for READY)  3. `td_run` for tests and builds (brief)  4. `td_logs` with `new: true`, `errors` or `grep`  5. `td_status` with `since`  6. `td_down`.

## Same thing from a shell

`tdk status`, `tdk up <app> --wait`, `tdk wait <app> <terminal> --match "Local:"`, `tdk logs <app> <terminal> --errors`, `tdk run <app> --brief -- npm test`, `tdk git <app> status`. Add `--json` for raw JSON. `tdk help` lists everything.
